repositories.description: Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first AI team for your desktop: a Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes, with projects, scheduled automations and connectors. Free app for macOS & Windows; built-in models or your own keys.
repositories.readme:
# Orkas **An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.** Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the **Commander** what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent** — to work on it together. Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A **project** holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. **To-dos** split the work between people and agents, **Auto-advance** lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and **scheduled automations** repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business. **[⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. [![Download for macOS & Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-macOS%20%26%20Windows-5b57d6?style=for-the-badge)](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](./LICENSE) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Orkas-AI/Orkas?style=flat&logo=github&label=Stars&color=yellow)](https://github.com/Orkas-AI/Orkas/stargazers) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Orkas-AI/Orkas?color=blue)](https://github.com/Orkas-AI/Orkas/releases) [![X: @leochenpm](https://img.shields.io/badge/X-%40leochenpm-black?logo=x)](https://x.com/leochenpm) [![Website: orkas.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-orkas.ai-5b57d6)](https://orkas.ai/?source=gh-orkas) [English](./README.md) · [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) --- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f8b16c8-a192-45a4-b19f-80e8d02c3dab ![Orkas desktop — task conversation and deliverables](./resources/app-ui/task-en.png) --- ## What the team delivers - **Videos, voice-overs and images** — VideoStudio, VoiceStudio, ImageStudio - **Research reports, SEO audits and market analysis** — DeepResearcher, SeoGeoAgent, StockAnalyser - **Posts, articles, newsletters and slide decks** — ContentWriter, PptMaker - **Websites, UI and code** — UIDesigner, ProductDeveloper - **Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files** — OfficeWorker - **E-commerce work** — product research, listings, review analysis, sales analysis and catalog changes, from five e-commerce agents - **Complex work that takes several agents** — the Commander splits it up, hands each part to the right agent and combines the results; for example, market research that becomes a report, a slide deck and a launch video 16 specialists ship with the app, each with its own skills, memory and tools. Browse 30+ agents in the [agent marketplace](https://orkas.ai/views/marketplace/gs/agents/?source=gh-orkas), or describe the role you need and the Commander builds a custom agent for you.
All 16 built-in agents | Area | Agent | What it delivers | | --- | --- | --- | | Research & analysis | **DeepResearcher** | Evidence-grounded research with verified sources, flagged contradictions and an auditable report | | | **SeoGeoAgent** | Give it a URL — technical audit, content quality, Core Web Vitals, AI-answer (GEO) citability, ranked fix list | | | **StockAnalyser** | Equity research, factor screens, backtests and portfolio risk checks, with traceable dashboards | | Content & media | **ContentWriter** | Publish-ready posts, articles, newsletters and case studies from a goal, sources or a rough draft | | | **PptMaker** | Editable, reviewable PPTX decks from a topic, outline or document | | | **ImageStudio** | Posters, covers, social images and infographics | | | **VideoStudio** | Narration, AI presenters, captions and dubbing, highlight clips, localization, and reference-video recreation with your own content and footage | | | **VoiceStudio** | Narration, multi-voice audio, transcripts and subtitles, audio editing and mixing | | | **UIDesigner** | Editable, HTML-first UI from product goals, PRDs, screenshots or Figma material | | Build & office | **ProductDeveloper** | Repo-aware engineering — implement a PRD, fix bugs, refactor, review, with verifiable results | | | **OfficeWorker** | Create, edit, check and deliver Word / Excel / PowerPoint / PDF files, one at a time or in batches | | E-commerce | **ECommerceResearcher** | Product selection by budget, market and sourcing limits — candidates, rejection reasons, validation plans | | | **ECommerceWriter** | Titles, detail pages, FAQs, image copy and video scripts in your brand voice | | | **ECommerceReviewer** | Review and reputation analysis — customer themes, root causes of bad reviews, priorities | | | **ECommerceAnalyzer** | Sales, profit, ads, refunds and inventory from your exports — reconciled metrics and decisions | | | **ECommerceOperator** | Plans catalog, price, promotion and inventory changes; executes only through tools you connect | More on each agent → [orkas.ai/agents](https://orkas.ai/agents/?source=gh-orkas)
### Recreate a reference video with your own content **VideoStudio** can recreate a viral video's narrative structure, visual style and editing pace using your own product, script and footage. Supply a reference video file and your assets: the agent analyzes the hook, information order, visual beats and call to action, then proposes what to preserve and what to replace before production. This works best for motion-graphic explainers, SaaS or app demos, and product ads built from your existing footage. Locally authored text, captions, narration and clips can be revised separately; text baked into AI-generated footage requires changing that footage. > "Use reference.mp4 as a reference for a 30-second vertical promo. Keep its hook, typography and pacing, replace the content with my product and screen recordings, and show me the breakdown and plan first." Start with a video file the agent can read; social-platform share-link downloading is not built in. Exact camera moves, human performances and frame-by-frame matching are not guaranteed. See the [reference-recreation workflow](./resources/builtin/marketplace/agents/79df9cc89f5f/skills/video-craft/references/reference-recreation.md). --- ## Keep the work moving One task is a good start. Orkas is built for the work that keeps going. - **Projects** — goals & rules, memory and files that every conversation in the project starts from, so you never brief from scratch. - **To-dos and Auto-advance** — every project has a to-do list for people and agents; with Auto-advance on, the team picks up the next item on its own and brings finished work back for your review. - **Scheduled automations** — run any task hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. Orkas runs on your computer. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts. - **Connectors** — Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets and Drive, Notion, Slack, Shopify, Stripe and many more. By default, Orkas asks before it sends, posts or deletes anything. - **Apps** — describe a tool and Orkas builds it as a local app inside the desktop app. In the packaged app, paid plans can also publish it as a web app with a public link. - **Shared projects** *(packaged app)* — invite a teammate or VA, and give each to-do to a person or an agent. > [!NOTE] > Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing are only in the packaged app — the open-source build doesn't support them yet. To use them, **[download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** (free, with 500 credits to start). Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an **Orkas API Key** in **Settings → Models**, then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. Audio is sent to Orkas for recognition and uses the key owner’s Orkas credits. Click again to stop, review the text, and send it yourself. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings. --- ## Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents **Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode**, and the personal agents **OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent**. The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way. [Using Claude Code and Codex together →](https://orkas.ai/blog/claude-code-codex-together/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Why Orkas - **A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest** — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit. - **Local-first by design** — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Cloud sync is optional in the packaged app. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model runs through Orkas's managed model service. - **Any model, switch any time** — the Commander and built-in agents share one model setting: the built-in Orkas model, your own provider, or a local endpoint. External CLI agents keep their own model settings. - **Agents that get better** — each agent keeps private skills and memory. Background reviews examine new activity when the app is idle and can refine self-assessment, reusable methods and learned skills. - **Open source, no black box** — MIT licensed. Read exactly what Orkas and every agent and skill do. > ⭐ If Orkas is useful to you, a star helps more people find the project. --- ## Download | | Packaged app (recommended) | Run from source | | --- | --- | --- | | Platforms | macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon & Intel), Windows 10+ | macOS, Windows, glibc 2.34+ Linux x64/arm64 | | Account | Sign in — 500 free credits | None | | Models | Built-in Orkas model, or your own keys | Your own keys or a local endpoint | | Also includes | Project collaboration, app publishing, cloud sync, and more | — | | Get it | **[Download Orkas](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** | [Quick start](#quick-start) | The download link detects your system and starts the right installer. --- ## What people use it for - **Marketing content** — launch videos, product pages, posts and newsletters in your voice. [Content writing](https://orkas.ai/use/content-writing/?source=gh-orkas) · [Videos](https://orkas.ai/use/make-videos/?source=gh-orkas) - **Store operations** — weekly sales briefs, review replies, listings and competitor checks. [E-commerce](https://orkas.ai/use/ecommerce/?source=gh-orkas) - **Research and reports** — sourced reports and decks, on demand or every week. [Research](https://orkas.ai/use/researchers/?source=gh-orkas) · [Data analysis](https://orkas.ai/use/data-analysis/?source=gh-orkas) - **Chat with your documents** — answers grounded in your own files, with citations back to the source passages. [Chat with documents](https://orkas.ai/use/chat-with-documents/?source=gh-orkas) - **Client work** — meeting briefs, monthly client reports and update decks in your template. [Monthly client report template](https://orkas.ai/blog/monthly-client-report-template/?source=gh-orkas) - **Product launch** — landing pages, bug fixes with tests, changelogs and launch posts. [Developers](https://orkas.ai/use/developers/?source=gh-orkas) - **Build an app** — quote calculators, booking forms, internal tools. [Build apps](https://orkas.ai/use/build-apps/?source=gh-orkas) - **Small teams** — one project for people and agents. [Small teams](https://orkas.ai/use/small-teams/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## How Orkas compares | Tool | What it is | How Orkas differs | | --- | --- | --- | | **Claude Code** | Anthropic's agentic coding tool — in the terminal, IDE, desktop and web, built on Claude models. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Claude Code as one of its agents. Around it, Orkas adds a model-agnostic team for the work beyond code — research, content, video and more — with projects, to-dos and automations that keep it moving. [Orkas vs Claude Code →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code/?source=gh-orkas) | | **Codex** | OpenAI's coding agent — in the terminal, your editor and the cloud. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Codex as one of its agents, next to Claude Code and OpenCode. The Commander can hand the coding to Codex and the review to another agent, then cover the non-code half of a release — docs, launch posts and videos. [Orkas vs Codex →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex/?source=gh-orkas) | | **LangChain** | A developer framework/library for building LLM apps and agents — code-first, embedded in your own Python/JS app. | Orkas is a desktop app you direct through chat, not by writing orchestration code. Data stays local by default. | | **CrewAI** | A Python framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous agents — you define crews and agents in code. | Orkas brings multi-agent orchestration into a desktop app, with projects, to-dos, automations and per-agent self-improvement built in. | | **OpenClaw** | A personal-agent platform with messaging integrations, multi-agent routing and sub-agents. | Orkas provides a desktop workspace for finished deliverables, with built-in specialists and coordination across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents. OpenClaw can join that workflow as a CLI agent. | | **Hermes-Agent** | Nous Research's self-improving agent — one agent with memory and skills, available as a CLI, a messaging gateway and a desktop app. | Orkas coordinates a team: the Commander directs many specialists and other CLI agents, and Hermes-Agent plugs in as one of them. | **Orkas is for you if** you want a team of agents rather than one assistant, work that keeps moving across days, and your data, keys and agents on your own disk. **Not for you if** you just want a single all-purpose chatbot, or a pure code library to embed in your own app. **Choosing between coding agents?** [Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code vs Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-vs-codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code alternatives](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-alternatives/?source=gh-orkas) **Full side-by-side comparisons →** [vs Claude Code](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Codex](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Cline](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-cline?source=gh-orkas) · [vs LangChain](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-langchain?source=gh-orkas) · [vs ChatGPT](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-chatgpt?source=gh-orkas) · [vs OpenClaw](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-openclaw?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Hermes-Agent](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-hermes-agent?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Quick start Want a packaged installer instead? See [Download](#download) above. To run from source — currently the way to run Orkas on Linux: **Requirements**: Node 22.12+ · macOS / Windows 10+ / glibc 2.34+ Linux x64 or arm64. Keep Python 3 and a C/C++ build toolchain available for the uncommon native-module source-build fallback. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Orkas-AI/Orkas.git cd Orkas ./run.sh # macOS / Linux run.cmd # Windows ``` Linux source runs require glibc 2.34+. Alpine and other musl-based distributions are not supported. Local speech transcription downloads and verifies the target-native whisper.cpp runtime and multilingual model during the first source launch. `run.sh` / `run.cmd` installs the locked npm dependency tree and prepares the pinned Python, uv, Node, embedding model (~95 MB), OfficeCLI, FFmpeg, whisper.cpp, and multilingual speech model resources on first launch. Linux startup then verifies the platform-native modules and Whisper runtime under Electron's ABI before opening the app. OCR and Skill-specific Python packages are installed into isolated local environments when those features are first used. First launch creates a workspace under `~/.orkas/` (macOS / Linux) or `:\.orkas\` (Windows). Then open **Settings → AI Providers** to add an API key or OAuth. Native dependency errors: use Node.js 24 LTS (minimum 22.12.0), then run `npm run native:repair` from this checkout. This restores optional packages, repairs SQLite for Electron, prepares bundled Node for isolated image processing, and checks SQL, sqlite-vec and sharp before success. Use `npm run native:check` for a check without installation. See the [native dependency verification script](./scripts/verify-native-dependencies.cjs) for the checks performed. --- ## How it works ### Task routing The Commander handles general work itself and delegates specialist work through three tools: - **`dispatch_to`** runs a named agent and returns its result for continued work. It can wait for the result or run asynchronously and notify the Commander when the task finishes. - **`hand_off_to`** transfers the remaining work to a named agent and ends the current Commander turn. The agent delivers its own reply; an optional continuation lets the Commander resume a broader task afterward. - **`run_worker`** runs an anonymous, isolated sub-task and returns a private result. It does not receive conversation history or a named agent's skills. Named agent tasks and anonymous workers have separate concurrency controls. See the [dispatch implementation](./src/main/features/group_chat/bus.ts) and [execution locks](./src/main/util/locks.ts). ### Context management The runtime budgets context against the selected model's usable input capacity, accounting for prompts, tools and persistent runtime state. Completed dialogue uses a bounded recent-history window; long active tasks use checkpoints to condense earlier process messages while retaining recent work. File reads, file changes and command executions also have structured records that can survive context compaction. See [context budgets](./src/core-agent/src/agent/context-budget.ts), [session history and checkpoints](./src/core-agent/src/agent/session.ts) and [workspace records](./src/core-agent/src/agent/workspace-state.ts). ### Memory and the Library Durable notes keep user preferences, project facts and each agent's reusable knowledge in separate scopes. These notes are distinct from the Library's document index and the stored conversation history. The Library extracts documents into passages and stores a local SQLite vector index. Its embedding model runs on your machine; the `library` tool can list files, search relevant passages and read source content from the global or current-project Library. Earlier conversations are retrieved separately through `chat_history`. See [scoped memory](./src/main/features/memory.ts), [document extraction](./src/main/util/file_to_chunks.ts), [Library tools](./src/main/model/core-agent/kb-tools.ts) and [conversation retrieval](./src/main/model/core-agent/chat-history-tools.ts). ### Execution limits and recovery Session locks and concurrency limits bound parallel work. Tool-round budgets, progress checkpoints, repeated-call checks and phase-aware idle watchdogs help contain runs that stall or repeat work. Named agent tasks can be tracked and cancelled individually; an admitted or queued task is not treated as a completed result. See [actor budgets](./src/main/features/group_chat/actor-budgets.ts), the [agent runtime](./src/core-agent/src/agent/runner.ts) and the [desktop model adapter](./src/main/model/core-agent/client.ts). ### Learning from activity Background reviews examine new agent activity when the app is idle, subject to cooldowns and execution limits. A review may update an agent's self-assessment (`COMPETENCE.md`), reusable methods (`LEARNING_STRATEGIES.md`) or learned skills. Reviews depend on new activity rather than task count, and can conclude that there is nothing worth saving. See the [reflection scheduler](./src/main/features/reflection-orchestrator.ts) and [review prompt](./src/core-agent/src/evolution/metacognition.ts). --- ## FAQ **What is Orkas?** Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app. Its Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents — plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — to deliver finished files. Not a single chatbot, not a code framework, not a hosted SaaS. **Do I need an API key?** No. The packaged app comes with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model. After that, buy credits, choose a paid plan or add your own provider keys; provider charges are separate. **Is Orkas a local LLM?** No. Orkas runs on your machine and calls the models you choose — the built-in Orkas model, your own API keys, or a local model endpoint. It orchestrates agents and tools; it is not itself a model. **Can Orkas answer questions from my documents, with citations?** Yes. Add PDFs and documents to your local Library; Orkas can search them and answer with citations to source passages, so you can open the original and check. The index is built on your machine. **Can I use local models like Ollama or LM Studio?** Yes. Open **Account settings → Models → Chat → Add model → Custom**, select **OpenAI-compatible** or **Anthropic-compatible**, and enter the base URL, exact model ID, and API key. Choose the saved model from the task's model control. **Where are my API keys and data stored?** On your disk by default. Your own provider keys are encrypted locally and excluded from cloud sync. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model uses Orkas's managed service. Optional cloud sync and shared projects in the packaged app store the selected data on Orkas servers. [Security and data handling →](https://orkas.ai/security/?source=gh-orkas) **Does Orkas work offline?** The source build can run fully offline against a local model endpoint. The packaged app needs to sign in, and cloud models need a network connection. **Does it keep working when my computer is off?** No — Orkas runs on your computer, so Auto-advance and automations need the computer awake and Orkas running. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts. **Can I build and publish apps?** Yes. Local apps that run inside Orkas are free. Publishing a web app to a public link needs a paid plan (Lite 5, Pro 8, Max 15 apps), and published web apps don't include every capability available inside Orkas. **Do I need an Orkas account?** The packaged desktop app asks you to sign in when you first launch it. The source build in this repository has no account layer at all — it boots straight into the app. **Can Orkas drive Claude Code and other CLI agents?** Yes. Orkas can drive five external CLI agents as local subprocesses — the coding agents Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, plus the personal agents OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — and onboard open-source projects like HyperFrames, all directed from the same chat. **How is Orkas different from Claude Code / Codex / CrewAI / LangChain?** Claude Code and Codex are coding agents — Orkas runs both as members of its team, so you don't have to choose between them; CrewAI and LangChain are code-first frameworks. Orkas is an open-source desktop app where a Commander coordinates a team of specialist agents and your CLI agents, with any model provider, and keeps data and keys local. See the [full comparisons](https://orkas.ai/compare/?source=gh-orkas). **Which platforms does Orkas support?** macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows 10+ have packaged installers. glibc 2.34+ Linux x64/arm64 runs from source today, with no installer yet. Local speech transcription is supported on Linux through the pinned whisper.cpp runtime prepared on first launch. Alpine and other musl-based distributions are not supported. The source bootstrap needs Node 22.12+; Python 3 and a C/C++ build toolchain are needed only when a native npm package has no compatible prebuilt binary and must be rebuilt locally. **Is Orkas free and open source?** Yes — the app is MIT licensed and free to use. The packaged app includes 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model; paid plans from $11.99/month add monthly credits, cloud sync, more shared projects and app publishing. With your own keys, model usage is billed by your provider; Orkas does not add a markup. [Pricing →](https://orkas.ai/pricing/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

repositories.description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal
repositories.readme:
Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer.


If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE.
If you want the desktop app experience, run codex app or visit the Codex App page.
If you are looking for the cloud-based agent from OpenAI, Codex Web, go to chatgpt.com/codex.

--- ## Quickstart ### Installing and running Codex CLI Run the following on Mac or Linux to install Codex CLI: ```shell curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh ``` Run the following on Windows to install Codex CLI: ```shell powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex" ``` The standalone installers download from `https://releases.openai.com/codex` by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable. To force GitHub Releases, set `CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM` to `false` (`0` and `no` are also accepted): ```shell curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh ``` ```powershell $env:CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM='false'; irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex ``` Codex CLI can also be installed via the following package managers: ```shell # Install using npm npm install -g @openai/codex ``` ```shell # Install using Homebrew brew install --cask codex ``` Then simply run `codex` to get started.
You can also go to the latest GitHub Release and download the appropriate binary for your platform. Each GitHub Release contains many executables, but in practice, you likely want one of these: - macOS - Apple Silicon/arm64: `codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - x86_64 (older Mac hardware): `codex-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - Linux - x86_64: `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` - arm64: `codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`), so you likely want to rename it to `codex` after extracting it.
### Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan Run `codex` and select **Sign in with ChatGPT**. We recommend signing into your ChatGPT account to use Codex as part of your Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan. [Learn more about what's included in your ChatGPT plan](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-codex-in-chatgpt). You can also use Codex with an API key, but this requires [additional setup](https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth#sign-in-with-an-api-key). ## Docs - [**Codex Documentation**](https://developers.openai.com/codex) - [**Contributing**](./docs/contributing.md) - [**Installing & building**](./docs/install.md) - [**Open source fund**](./docs/open-source-fund.md) This repository is licensed under the [Apache-2.0 License](LICENSE).

repositories.readme:
Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

The AI Orchestrator for 100x builders.
Run Codex, ClaudeCode, OpenCode or Pi side-by-side — each in its own worktree, tracked in one place.

Download Orca

## Features
### Mobile Companion Monitor and steer your agents from your phone — get notified when an agent finishes and send follow-ups from anywhere. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Android APK](https://www.onorca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Parallel Worktrees Fan one prompt across five agents, each in its own isolated git worktree — compare the results and merge the winner. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Terminal Splits Ghostty-class terminals with WebGL rendering, infinite splits, and scrollback that survives restarts. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/terminal)
### Design Mode Click any UI element in a real Chromium window to send its HTML, CSS, and a cropped screenshot straight into your agent's prompt. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native Browse PRs, issues, and project boards in-app — open a worktree from any task and review without a context switch. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### SSH Worktrees Run agents on a beefy remote box with full file editing, git, and terminals — auto-reconnect and port forwarding included. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/ssh)
### Annotate AI Diffs Drop comments on any diff line and ship them back to the agent — review, edit, and commit without leaving Orca. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Drag Files to Agents VS Code's editor with autosave everywhere — drag files or images straight into an agent prompt. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)
### Orca CLI Agents drive Orca too — script every workflow with `orca worktree create`, `snapshot`, `click`, and `fill`. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
**Also in the box:** - **[Quick open](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)** — Search across worktrees, files, agents, commands, and repo context without leaving your flow. - **[Account switcher & usage tracking](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)** — See Claude and Codex usage and rate-limit resets, and hot-swap accounts without re-logging in. - **[Rich repo previews](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/editing/markdown)** — Preview Markdown, images, PDFs, and repo docs in the workspace. - **[Computer Use](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)** — Let agents operate desktop apps and visible UI when a workflow needs real interaction. - **[Notifications and unread state](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/notifications)** — Know when an agent finishes or needs attention, then mark threads unread to come back later. - **And many, many more** — we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

--- ## Install ### Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux - **[Download from onOrca.dev](https://onorca.dev/download)** - Or grab a build directly: [macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-arm64.dmg) · [macOS Intel](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-x64.dmg) · [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-windows-setup.exe) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-linux.AppImage) · [All builds](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest) _Or via a package manager:_ ```bash # macOS (Homebrew) # Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask. brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Upgrade an existing install brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source yay -S stably-orca-bin ``` ### Mobile Companion — iOS, Android Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone. - **iOS:** [Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) - **Android:** [Download APK](https://www.onorca.dev/download/android) · [Install guide](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/android-apk) --- ## Community & Support - **Discord:** Join the community on **[Discord](https://discord.gg/fzjDKHxv8Q)**. - **Twitter / X:** Follow **[@orca_build](https://x.com/orca_build)** for updates and announcements. - **WeChat:** Scan to join the Orca community WeChat group. - **Feedback & Ideas:** We ship fast. Missing something? [Request a new feature](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues). - **Privacy:** See the [privacy & telemetry docs](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/telemetry) for what anonymous usage data Orca collects and how to opt out. - **Show Support:** [Star](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) this repo to follow along with our daily ships. --- ## Developing Want to contribute or run locally? See our [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. The relay that pairs the mobile app with a desktop host is also in this repository under [`cloud/`](cloud/README.md), with a separate pnpm workspace and setup guide.

repositories.name: taste-skill
repositories.description: Agent skills that give coding agents taste: art direction, reference images and a browser check instead of generic AI pages
repositories.readme:
Sponsors

interfaces.dev · A design engineering magazine by Jakub Krehel
React Bits · animated React components for creative interfaces
IMG.LY · CreativeEditor SDK
Sent.dm · messaging APIs for SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS

Become a sponsor

**Taste Skill** is an Agent Skill that makes coding agents design websites and app screens instead of assembling the average landing page. It gives the agent an art direction, real pictures and a way to check its own work in a real browser. Pages it has built, each from one brief:
The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ([credits](examples/v2/CREDITS.md)). Watch the [launch film](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/releases/tag/v2.0.0). ## Install ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend" ``` That installs the skill with the [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) CLI. The skill runs its scripts with **Node 22+** and an installed **Chrome, Edge or Chromium**. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Finding pictures needs network access.
Claude Code plugin Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under `taste-skill:`, so it does not collide with your other skills. ``` /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill /plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill ``` `/plugin update` upgrades it later.
Codex plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill ``` Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skill is loaded.
From a clone, linked instead of copied `./install.sh` symlinks the skill into Claude Code (`--codex` for Codex, `--all-agents` for both), so a `git pull` updates it in place.
Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See [Moved skills](#moved-skills). ## How v2 works The skill is built from a study of 247 curated sites. A build runs in six steps: 1. Reads the brief and lists what only this client has. 2. A script deals three of 20 researched directions and the agent picks one. 3. Finds the idea: one sentence tying the client's own material to that direction. 4. Builds with real pictures and footage from open collections, credited. 5. Checks the page in a real browser at three widths and fails it on slop. 6. Looks at its own screenshots and fixes the top three problems, up to three rounds. A build takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes and a few hundred thousand tokens. Details are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and the [study](skills/taste-skill/references/research.md). Dashboards and app screens (v2.1) take their own route: the skill deals one of the app styles distilled from real product screens, builds the shell, the data, the charts and the tables to those numbers, and checks the result with app rules: quiet panels, aligned figures, colour spent on data, a phone layout where the navigation folds away. A product's landing page builds the app it shows the same way, so its screenshots look like a working product. v2.1 also checks the frame of every page (a clear title on the first screen, equal margins, no section shoved to one side, no random blank stretches) and moves the way strong award sites do, measured on the latest 100 Awwwards Sites of the Day. ## Moved skills This repo holds one skill, `design-taste-frontend`. The others moved to repos of their own and kept their install names: | Install name | Where it lives now | | --- | --- | | `high-end-visual-design`, `minimalist-ui`, `industrial-brutalist-ui`, `gpt-taste`, `stitch-design-taste`, `design-taste-frontend-v1`, `design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental` | **[Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics)** | | `imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, `brandkit`, `image-to-code` | **[Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills)** | | `redesign-existing-projects` | Part of `design-taste-frontend`, which audits an existing page in a real browser before changing anything | | `full-output-enforcement` | Removed. For the same problem, see **[Leonxlnx/unlazy](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/unlazy)** | Install a moved skill from its new repo under the same name: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics --skill "high-end-visual-design" ``` ## Common Questions **What does the skill need?** Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. It installs nothing and uses no API keys. It needs the internet only to find pictures. **Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?** From open collections such as Wikimedia Commons, Openverse and the Met. Only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA files are offered, and the skill puts the credits on the page. Replace them with your own when you have them. **Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?** Yes. The rules are about design, not a framework. **Is it for dashboards and app screens?** Yes, since v2.1. The skill tells a page from an app screen and builds a dashboard, an admin view or a settings screen with its own run: a style dealt from a study of real product screens, quiet panels, honest data and charts, and its own checks (`inspect.mjs --app`). ## Support the project If Taste Skill helps you, consider sponsoring: [Sponsor on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/Leonxlnx) ### Open Source Supporters

Get a Kimi API key: taste-skill users get 10% bonus API credits on their first purchase.
### Community Sponsors

Feedback: open an issue or pull request, DM [@lexnlin](https://x.com/lexnlin) or [@blueemi99](https://x.com/blueemi99), or email [hello@tasteskill.dev](mailto:hello@tasteskill.dev). Taste Skill has no official token, coin, or crypto project. Any token using my name, image, or project is unaffiliated and not endorsed by me. ## License [MIT License](LICENSE) · Copyright (c) 2026 Leonxlnx

repositories.name: openGym
repositories.description: Open-source gym & body-weight tracker, now in the App Store (iPhone + Apple Watch) and as an Android APK. Plan routines, log workouts, see which muscles are trained, import from Strong/Hevy/FitNotes. Self-host it or use it on the phone alone.
repositories.readme:
[Website](https://opengym.ch) · [Live demo](https://opengym.ch/demo/) · [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
## Why openGym Most workout apps keep your data on their servers, push you towards a subscription, or vanish when the company does. openGym runs on your own box, keeps your data in a folder you control, and is yours to fork. It still behaves like a modern app: installable on the home screen, passkey sign-in, works offline, syncs between your phone and your laptop. No account on someone else's server, no subscription, no ads, no telemetry. One `docker compose up` and it's running. The [in-browser demo](https://opengym.ch/demo/) is the real app with example data, if you want to try it before installing anything. ## Features **Planning** - A routine per weekday over a library of **over 5,600 exercises** with animated demos, searchable and browsable by muscle on a body map. Filter by the equipment you own. - Four starter plans (Push/Pull/Legs, Upper/Lower, Full Body, 5×5) that load as ordinary, editable routines. - Every session on the Plan page and today's on Home carries a tiny body map with the muscles it works lit up, so you know Leg Day is legs before you open it. - Move a session to another day without touching the weekly plan. The week starts on Monday or Sunday, your choice. - Or skip the weekdays altogether: a **rotation** (A, B, C, A, ...) where the next session is simply the next one you haven't done, however the week went. - Supersets, warm-up sets, drop sets and rest-pause, timed exercises (planks, hangs, carries), cardio by time and speed, rest time per exercise, planned deloads. - Your own exercises, with your own photo, GIF or short video. Location data is stripped on the device before upload. **Training** - Guided sessions: today's workout starts itself, weights are pre-filled from last time, a rest timer runs between sets, PRs are detected as you go. On a rest day it tells you when the next session is. - A quiet workout screen: one menu per exercise, the set number as the set's own menu, card or list view. Switches in Settings bring the old button rows back if you liked them. - Optional effort column as RIR or RPE, colour-coded, with a plain-language line per level. - Plate math for barbell, EZ bar, trap bar and Smith machine, worked out from the plates you own. - Bodyweight exercises know they carry no load: log reps, add a dip belt if you use one. - Per-side reps for lunges and single-arm work, the screen stays awake while you train, and a rest-timer alert can flash the screen for loud gyms. - Swipe a set left to delete it (with Undo) or right to copy it. Pyramid sets with their own reps and rest per set, and a scroll wheel for any rest time up to 15 minutes, or no timer at all. - Machine taken? A planned backup exercise swaps in with one tap and keeps the slot's sets and reps. Machines can carry their real weight stack, odd steps included, and progression sticks to it. - The session's volume runs live at the end of the progress bar. **Progress** - Progression rules per routine or per exercise: linear, Greyskull LP, double progression through a visible rep range, triple progression (reps, then sets, then load), or adding time. Each target explains why it is that number; missed reps never add load, stalls trigger a deload. - Estimated 1RM per exercise with its own curve, Structural Balance ratios (Poliquin, Thibaudeau, ATG), a year-long activity heatmap. - A muscle map in three modes: where your volume went, what is still recovering, and what has gone untrained. - Body-weight chart against a goal line, with your weekly rate and an optional lose, gain or hold range, and progress photos on a timeline with a before/after slider. - Lifts as a percentage of body weight, and a running total of everything you've ever lifted. - Edit any saved workout after the fact, log one you did on paper, or move it to the right date. Records are re-read from the corrected history. **Accounts and data** - Passkeys (Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint) with per-profile data synced across devices. Password sign-in can be switched on per instance; new devices pair with a one-time code or QR. - Two devices editing at once merge field by field instead of overwriting each other (see [sync](#how-sync-works)). - Import from FitNotes, Strong, Hevy (CSV or API key) and Apple Health weight exports. Export everything as one JSON file, or your workouts and body data as a spreadsheet (CSV). - Share a plan as a small file or print it as a PDF. - Optional admin dashboard with invite-only signup and an activity log. - 20 languages, including right-to-left Arabic and Traditional Chinese. Exercise names and instructions are translated for most of them. **On the phone and the wrist** - Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android that work on their own (no server, no account) or connected to yours. Rest timer in the notification shade, reminders, and Health Connect or Apple Health in both directions: workouts go out, weigh-ins and heart rate per set come back in. - A gym reminder, off by default: walk into one of your gyms and the phone nudges you to hit Start. Once a day at most, never after you trained, and your gyms stay on the phone. - An Apple Watch app: tick off sets with the Digital Crown, RPE or RIR right on the wrist, a full-screen rest countdown, heart rate per set, a Lock button against stray crown presses, and complications. - Widgets and a Live Activity on the iPhone: log a set, skip the rest or jump to the next exercise from the Lock Screen without opening the app. **Optional extras, off by default** - An [AI coach](docs/AI_COACH.md) that drafts a week of routines and later suggests changes based on what you logged, and answers questions about your training. You approve every change. It runs on your server, or on the phone alone, with your own provider key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama included). - An [MCP server](mcp/README.md) so an assistant like Claude Desktop can answer questions about your training history, and log a workout you describe to it. Local; not part of the Docker build. The full list of what changed release by release is in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ## Quick start You need [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) with Compose. ```bash git clone https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym cd openGym cp .env.example .env docker compose pull # prebuilt images, amd64 + arm64 (skip this to build from source) docker compose up -d ``` Open , tap **Create profile**, and you're in. The exercise animations are part of the image, so there's nothing else to download. To reach it from your phone with passkeys you need HTTPS on a domain; that's a two-line change in `.env`. The [self-hosting guide](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) walks through Cloudflare Tunnel, Caddy, Traefik and nginx, and there are separate guides for [HTTPS on a LAN](docs/SELF_HOSTING_HTTPS.md), [a Mac with Tailscale](docs/SELF_HOSTING_MAC.md) and [Kubernetes](docs/SELF_HOSTING_KUBERNETES.md). > [!NOTE] > Images are published from the same tag to `ghcr.io/duartesantos8/opengym-{api,web}` > (what `docker-compose.yml` pulls) and `registry.gitlab.com/duartesantos8/opengym/{api,web}`. Swap > the `image:` lines if you prefer GitLab's registry, or run `docker compose up -d --build` to build > locally. Either way you don't need Node on the host.
Configuration reference (all through .env) | Variable | What it does | Default | |---|---|---| | `RP_ID` | Hostname passkeys are bound to | `localhost` | | `ORIGIN` | Full URL the app is served from | `http://localhost:8080` | | `WEB_PORT` | Host port for the web UI | `8080` | | `NGINX_PORT` | Port the web container listens on inside the container | `80` | | `BACKEND` | Name of the API service that `/api` is proxied to | `api` | | `PORT` | Port the API listens on; the web container proxies to the same value | `3000` | | `RP_NAME` | Name shown in the passkey prompt | `openGym` | | `SESSION_DAYS` | How long a sign-in lasts, in days | `90` | | `ADMIN_UIDS` | User ids that get the admin dashboard, comma-separated | *(none)* | | `FIRST_USER_ADMIN` | `1`: the first profile created on an empty instance becomes its admin | *(off)* | | `INVITE_ONLY` | Require an invite code to create a profile | *(off)* | | `ALLOW_GUEST` | Offer "Continue without account"; `0` requires a profile | *(on)* | | `PASSWORD_LOGIN` | Offer name-and-password sign-in next to passkeys | *(off)* | | `TRUST_PROXY` | Let the sign-in throttle read the client address from proxy headers | `1` in `docker-compose.yml` | | `AUDIT_LOG` | Record sign-ins and admin actions; `0` records nothing | *(on)* | | `AUDIT_MAX` | Events kept in the activity log; `0` for no limit | `5000` | | `AUDIT_DAYS` | Days kept in the activity log; `0` keeps until `AUDIT_MAX` | `90` | | `AUDIT_IP` | Record the caller's address: `off`, `net` (network only) or `full` | `off` | | `ALLOWED_PRIVATE_IPS` | Private addresses push endpoints may resolve to (FakeDNS, split-horizon DNS): comma-separated IPs, `a-b` ranges or CIDR blocks | *(none)* | | `VAPID_SUBJECT` | Contact URL sent with push notifications | your `ORIGIN` | | `API_TARGET` | API image to build: `default`, or `coach` with the Claude Agent SDK and Codex CLI | `default` | | `COACH_DISABLED` | `1` forces the AI coach off instance-wide | *(unset)* | Push-notification keys are generated on first run into `./data/vapid.json`. `DATA_DIR` is pinned to `/data` inside the container and mapped to `./data` on the host; change the volume, not the variable. The [self-hosting guide](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) covers every option in detail.
## Phone app The same codebase builds the phone apps with Capacitor. Use them on their own (everything stays on the phone, no account) or connect them to your server and sync. | | Get it | |---|---| | **iPhone and iPad**, with the **Apple Watch** app | The [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6822275400), in every App Store country | | **Android** | The signed APK from the [latest release](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym/releases/latest) or [opengym.ch](https://opengym.ch), in three sizes: **Standard** (`openGym-X.Y.Z.apk`, animations at 180 px, about 315 MB), **Plus** (`openGym-Plus-X.Y.Z.apk`, 240 px, about 424 MB) and **HD** (`openGym-HD-X.Y.Z.apk`, 360 px, about 760 MB). It updates itself and stays the kind you picked | | **Google Play** | Coming: a new developer account has to run a closed test first | Every APK sits next to its `.sha256`. The APK and the Play app share one signing key, so you can switch between them (or between Standard, Plus and HD) without losing data. Details, building it yourself and connecting to your server: [docs/MOBILE.md](docs/MOBILE.md). ## How it works

- **`frontend/`** is React 19 and Vite (React Router, Zustand), built to static files inside Docker. - **`api/`** is plain `node:http` with three dependencies: `@simplewebauthn/server` for passkeys, `web-push` for notifications and `undici` for the AI coach's provider calls. Everything is stored as JSON under `./data`. - **`web/`** builds the frontend and serves it with nginx, proxying `/api` so the whole app sits on one origin, which passkeys require. The [architecture overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) has the longer version, with diagrams of the frontend, sync, the exercise media and the watch. The training logic (progression rules, 1RM, how a logged session is read back) lives in pure functions under `frontend/src/lib/` with tests beside them. The HTTP API is documented as an OpenAPI spec in [`api/openapi.yaml`](api/openapi.yaml), browsable at [opengym.ch/api.html](https://opengym.ch/api.html). ### How sync works Each profile's data is one document with a server revision. A device sends the revision it last saw along with its changes; if another device wrote in between, the server refuses and returns the current document so the device can merge and retry. Every change carries its own stamp, down to a single setting or routine field, so the merge keeps the newest edit of each one and a deletion stays deleted.

Nothing that hasn't reached the server is discarded on disconnect or sign-out, and the app shows a banner whenever it's working offline. ### Your data Everything lives in `./data` on your host: | File | Contents | |---|---| | `db.json` | Profiles and public passkey data | | `db.json.bak` | A copy of the last good `db.json`, used if the main file can't be read | | `state-.json` | Each user's plan, workouts, body weight and settings | | `audit.log` | Admin activity log (no IP addresses unless you turn that on) | | `secret` | Session-cookie signing key | Back up `./data` and you've backed up everything. Passkey private keys never reach the server; they stay in your phone's secure hardware or your password manager. ## Documentation The [documentation index](docs/README.md) sorts every guide by who it's for. The most used ones: | I want to | Read | |---|---| | Get a quick answer | [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md) | | Set up my own instance | [Self-hosting](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) | | Use the Android or iPhone app | [Phone app](docs/MOBILE.md) | | Bring my history from another app | [Importing data](docs/DATA_IMPORTS.md) | | Turn on the AI coach | [AI coach](docs/AI_COACH.md) | | Contribute code | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | Report a security problem | [Security](SECURITY.md) | ## Roadmap A release roughly every one to two weeks, each one whatever has passed testing by then. The full plan is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), and the issues sit in the [GitHub milestones](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym/milestones). | Release | When | Theme | |---|---|---| | v1.4.0 | released Oct 2026 | A new exercise database with 5,632 exercises, plus two rounds of community work | | v1.4.1 | released Oct 2026 | Bug fixes for v1.4.0 | | v1.4.2 | released Oct 2026 | The App Store, the Apple Watch, widgets, three APK sizes | | v1.4.3 | released Oct 2026 | The Halloween and community release: gym reminder, health data read back, watch upgrades, CSV export | | v1.4.4 | Nov 2026 | Programmes, a tour with tutorials, AirPods heart rate, kg or lb per exercise, bug fixes | | v1.4.5 | Nov 2026 | Google Play, F-Droid, Settings → Integrations (Strava, webhooks, calendar, Nextcloud), timed holds that start themselves | | v1.4.6 | Dec 2026 | Wear OS, deeper Health Connect, body composition | | v1.4.7 | Dec 2026 | The progression engine by @giulioleuci, circuits, AMRAP and EMOM | | later | dates are guesses | Search and catalogue, accounts, a trainer role, skins, Garmin, database storage | ## Community - **[Discord](https://discord.gg/e62jY6fwVb)** for release announcements, self-hosting help and quick back-and-forth. Usually the fastest way to get an answer. - **[Discussions](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym/discussions)** for questions and ideas you want the next person to find by searching. - **[Issues](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym/issues)** for reproducible bugs and agreed-on work. Login trouble is almost always an `RP_ID`/`ORIGIN` mismatch; the [self-hosting guide](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) covers it. - **[Pull requests](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym/pulls)** are welcome; start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ### Where the code lives GitHub is the home of the project. [gitlab.com/DuarteSantos8/opengym](https://gitlab.com/DuarteSantos8/opengym) is a mirror, updated by a GitHub Actions workflow on every push to `main` and every release tag. It exists because its CI builds the multi-arch images and the SBOMs for its registry (the APKs are built and signed on the release machine and attached to the GitHub release). Nothing is merged there by hand. In the changelog, `!NN` refers to a GitLab merge request from the weeks in August and September 2026 when the project lived there. ## How openGym is built People have asked about this, so plainly: **openGym is developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)**, Anthropic's coding agent. A large share of the code, tests and documentation is drafted in Claude Code sessions, and the repository carries a [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) with the project context those sessions start from. What that does and doesn't mean: - **A person decides and ships.** What goes in, what gets reviewed and merged, and every release are the maintainer's call. Changes are tested on a staging instance and on real phones before they are tagged. - **Tests hold the logic in place.** The training logic is covered by unit tests, and pull requests run the frontend, API and MCP suites in CI. That is the guard against plausible-looking code that is wrong, whoever or whatever wrote it. - **The app itself doesn't need an LLM.** Nothing in a default install calls an AI service. The AI coach and the MCP server are opt-in, and the coach only talks to the provider you configure, with your own key. Community pull requests are written by their authors, with whatever tools they like, and reviewed the same way. ## Support openGym is free and stays free: AGPL, no paid tier, nothing held back for sponsors. If it replaced a paid tracker for you and you'd like to chip in, there's Buy Me a Coffee, Ko-fi and GitHub Sponsors (the app has the same three under Settings → About & updates, and on the iPhone a shortcut to leaving an App Store review). A star, a bug report or a pull request helps just as much. [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/DuarteSantos8) [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=duartesantos8/opengym&type=Date)](https://star-history.com/#DuarteSantos8/openGym&Date) ## License **openGym's own code** is licensed under the [GNU AGPL v3.0](LICENSE). You can self-host, use, modify and share it; if you run a modified version as a network service, you have to offer that version's source under the same license. > [!IMPORTANT] > **The exercise media is not covered by that license.** The stills and animations are > © Aliaksandr Makatserchyk, [Gym visual](https://gymvisual.com/), licensed for use in openGym only: > 180 px in this repository and on self-hosted servers, larger only inside the app packages. A > non-commercial fork may keep them unmodified with the notice; anything else needs your own licence > from gymvisual.com.
